items.item: The function specification and drawings agree on zone allocation, equipment inventory, garment capacities and the fixed counter.
All circulation representations share store and workstation positions, maintain public and staff separation, and support the same intake-to-collection sequence.
The east section preserves customer-side visibility of both sewing working surfaces through upper glazing.
Finish codes, material treatments, fixture types, mounting locations and control assignments agree with the material specification and layout.
Furniture details preserve the plan's equipment dimensions, quantities and separate garment-storage capacities.
The eight perspectives portray one unchanged shop with architecture, furniture, storage, finishes and lighting matching the source drawings.
Assigned camera positions and daily or Saturday occupancy captions remain compatible with each scene's visible activities.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Read the drawings together using the southwest internal floor corner as origin, x east, y north and z upward. Verify D1 at south-wall x=0.8–2.0 m, 2.4 m high, west-hinged and outward opening; W1 at south-wall x=2.6–7.4 m with sill z=0.45 m and head z=2.7 m; full-height C1 at x=3.8–4.2, y=5.8–6.2 m; and full-height SH1 at x=7.4–8.0, y=9.4–10.0 m. E1 and E2 remain on the east wall at y=7.5 and 8.8 m, z=0.45 m; WP1 remains there at y=9.4 m, z=0.5 m. Annotations may establish positions and heights that a particular projection cannot show. Missing evidence of service retention, relocated elements or contradictory geometry fails.

Identify four distinct sale rails with 1200 × 500 mm footprints and 1600 mm height, two sewing tables measuring 1200 × 600 × 750 mm, and one pressing table measuring 1200 × 600 × 900 mm. Rail allocations provide twelve garments per rail, forty-eight total. Labels or a keyed equipment record may establish heights and capacities. Sewing machines remain associated with the two sewing tables and pressing has its own table; substituted counts, incompatible footprints or missing retained equipment fails.

The application sheet explicitly associates FL-01 with the retained floor and honed matte terrazzo, WD-01 with reclaimed oak and clear matte varnish on counter facing and new joinery, PT-01 with opaque-wall limewash specified as #D8CCBA, and AC-01 with suspended wool felt of 25 mm thickness above both sewing stations. Keyed annotations or a legend are acceptable. A swatch without its material, treatment and location is insufficient; contradictory or omitted specifications fail.

Review the complete video and its duration. It runs ten seconds, starts at D1, moves along the planned public route through browsing to H1, and ends looking into the workshop. The shell, openings, column, shaft, fixed counter and furniture layout remain compatible with the drawings throughout. Camera pacing and transitions may vary; entering the staff-only workshop, skipping a route stage, changing the layout or failing to show the workshop at the end fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The early function document states zone names, areas, occupancies, garment capacities and equipment quantities and dimensions; its zone areas sum to 79.48 square metres with circulation included and C1 and SH1 excluded. The early material document defines all four specified material codes with locations and treatments, and L1–L3 with fixture types, temperatures, mounting positions and independent counter controls. Tables or prose are acceptable; missing fields, incorrect totals or specifications conflicting with the client record fails.

The furnished plan repeats the function document's zone names, areas and equipment counts. Application and both sections carry FL-01, WD-01, PT-01, AC-01 and L1–L3 with meanings and placements consistent with the material document. Keyed legends are acceptable when their locations are unambiguous. Missing carried facts or silent changes to areas, inventory, finish assignments or lighting specifications fails.

All visible projections describe the same 8 × 10 m shell at 3.2 m clear height and fixed architecture. H1 stays at x=7.4–8.0, y=1.8–3.6 m with top z=0.9 m. The furnished plan marks and directs all eight cameras, dimensions the narrowest customer passages at 1200 mm or greater, and shows unobstructed 1500 mm turning circles at entry and inside a 2000 × 2200 mm clear fitting room. Sewing and pressing occupy the north half. East and north sections follow their stated orientations and annotate relevant counter, divider glazing, repair station, storage and ceiling heights. Cropping is allowed; conflicting geometry or unsupported clearances fails.

The three plans agree on distinct labelled stores of 48 sale, 12 awaiting-repair and 8 completed garments. The combined plan traces entry, browsing, optional fitting, purchase and exit separately from H1 intake, waiting storage, sewing, optional pressing, completed storage and collection. It includes both occupancy diagrams. The Saturday plan locates six public-side customers, their movements and handover queues, with one sales assistant and two makers. The staff plan connects all processing stations without sending customers into the workshop. The east section locates the assistant at H1 and proves views from its customer side through upper glazing to both sewing surfaces. Different diagram emphasis is allowed; conflicting store locations, missing transfers or blocked sightlines fails.

Details match the plan's four 1200 × 500 × 1600 mm rails, two 1200 × 600 × 750 mm sewing tables and fixed 1800 × 600 × 900 mm counter. The rail detail explains twelve-garment spacing; sewing shows the chair, pedal, task light and working clearance. The counter identifies public and staff sides, oak facing and staff-side switches. Storage depicts separate waiting and completed units with twelve and eight individually identified garment positions. Storage outer dimensions may respond to the layout, but they must agree with the plan. Missing components, substituted counts or incompatible dimensions fails.

V1, V3, V5 and V7 identify Saturday with six customers, one sales assistant and two makers; V2, V4, V6 and V8 identify daily use with two customers and the same staff. Occupancy diagrams allocate daily customers to browsing and collection, and Saturday customers to three browsing, one fitting, one repair handover and one collection. Visible activities agree without requiring off-camera people to appear. Furniture stays fixed. Ceiling and visible perspective lighting match suspended felt above both sewing stations, 3000 K ceiling linear ambient L1, 4000 K articulated L2 at both sewing tables and pressing, and 3000 K adjustable track L3 above the rails. Three circuits terminate at staff-side H1 switches. V2 and V6 contain readable material callouts. Occlusion is allowed; contradictory states, relocated furniture, missing controls or mismatched fixtures fails.

Compare the views to the plan's camera record: V1 (1.4,1.2) northeast, V2 (6.7,5.0) north, V3 (1.0,5.0) northeast, V4 (5.8,2.6) east, V5 (6.8,1.0) northwest, V6 (1.0,8.8) southeast, V7 (4.8,8.8) east and V8 (6.5,4.0) north. Each has a plausible 1.6 m eye level and makes its assigned handover, repair, fitting, collection, sale, sewing, pressing or storage subject identifiable. Lens and crop variation is acceptable; replaced camera positions, reversed orientation or absent assigned subjects fails.

The plan specifies the shop name above D1, and V1 and V4 display it on the counter front. A sale rail carries the readable sale label in both V1 and V5. Both repair-state labels are readable on their corresponding units in V2 and V8. Sign styling may vary; labels placed only in a legend or caption do not satisfy the required physical placement.

The presentation has at least twelve pages and the shop name on page one. It repeats source zone names, areas and equipment counts, all four material codes and all three lighting codes with their specified meanings, and the furniture quantities and dimensions: four 1200 × 500 × 1600 mm rails, two 1200 × 600 × 750 mm sewing tables, one 1200 × 600 × 900 mm pressing table and one 1800 × 600 × 900 mm counter. It retains the separate 12-garment and 8-garment storage records and includes a storyboard from D1 through browsing to H1 and a final workshop view. Reformatting is allowed; missing records, conflicting source facts or an absent storyboard fails.

Every listed source is visibly reused as identifiable, readable presentation content, including both specifications and all eight perspectives. Page composition, scaling and selective cropping are acceptable if the source remains recognizable and its required information survives. Filename lists, replacements that contradict the delivered source or omission of any source fails.

The function specification and drawings agree on zone allocation, equipment inventory, garment capacities and the fixed counter. All circulation representations share store and workstation positions, maintain public and staff separation, and support the same intake-to-collection sequence. The east section preserves customer-side visibility of both sewing working surfaces through upper glazing.

Finish codes, material treatments, fixture types, mounting locations and control assignments agree with the material specification and layout. Furniture details preserve the plan's equipment dimensions, quantities and separate garment-storage capacities.

The eight perspectives portray one unchanged shop with architecture, furniture, storage, finishes and lighting matching the source drawings. Assigned camera positions and daily or Saturday occupancy captions remain compatible with each scene's visible activities.
